pages.en:
The instant I hear that much, I abruptly lose myself.

My body becomes a sheet of paper, folded smaller and smaller.

Slowly, carefully, I am put away. Yet time in the outer world has stopped, so from without the event must occur at the speed of light.

There is no end to the folding, no limit to the reduction. Any plane, however vast, can only be folded so many times, yet I continue closing inward upon myself.

My vision turns blue. The world before I was folded had been red.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s all I hear before suddenly losing sight of myself.
It feels like my body has turned into paper that is being folded up.
It’s being slowly, carefully put away. But time has stopped in the outside world, so from the outside it must look like it’s happening at the speed of light.
There’s no end to the stowing and reduction.
Any flat object should have a limit to how many times it can be folded no matter how wide its surface area, but my body is being shut up deeper and deeper.
My field of vision is turning blue. The world before I was folded up is red.

—Ah.

I realize that my arms were folded away long ago and no longer exist.

That is a problem. Everything unnecessary—everything I do not need here—has been stripped from me, but without limbs, I cannot even recognize myself.

Therefore my first task is not to examine the world, but to imagine a form for myself.

So the first thing I should do isn’t to affirm the world, but to hypothesize my own form.

I clench both hands.

Though the form is hypothetical, I can now perceive myself with certainty.

There is neither above nor below, neither sky nor earth. I float within a blue celestial sphere.

It is quiet—not in sound, but in form. Complete and perfectly still.

It’s peaceful. Not in terms of sound, but rather the entire shape is peaceful and complete.

Scantily clad, Tohsaka brings it down upon me in a succession of overhead blows.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She pursues me with the pillow.
Tohsaka hits me repeatedly with overhead swings of the pillow in her immodest state.

いいから止める！ ヘンだぞ、何がどうしたんだ！」

“W-wait, did you put magical energy into that thing!?

“Stop! You're acting crazy! What is wrong with you!?”

“Sh-shut up, you beast! You peer into a girl's secrets, and now you sit there looking so smug!”

“Ow—ah—wait! *That* was some enormous secret!?”

Just stop already! This is weird, what’s wrong with you?!”

「あ」
「ぎ」

I cry out in surprise, leaving a gap in my guard. The pillow connects directly with my face.

“Ah.”

“Gih—”

It is a rising pillow uppercut.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I shout in surprise, and receive a direct hit to the face from the opening in my guard.
“Ah.”
“Guh.”
An agonizing pillow uppercut.

遠坂はまだ怒り足りないのか、俺の後ろ首をむんずと掴んで、ずるずると床の上を引きずっていった。

pages.en:
Perhaps the transplant has exhausted me as well. Once again, I am knocked helplessly flat.

Still unsatisfied, Tohsaka seizes me by the back of the neck and drags me across the floor.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Combined with the fatigue from the transfer, I’m knocked down again.
Tohsaka must still be angry, as she grabs the back of my neck and drags me across the floor.

「
ふん。いいわよ、いつかこっちから恥ずかしい記憶を覗き返してやるんだから。その時は土下座をしても許さないわよ、ええ」
「それは勘弁……あれ、もしかして……」

pages.en:
“—Hmph. Fine. One day I'll peer into an embarrassing memory of yours in return. And when that happens, I won't forgive you even if you prostrate yourself before me.”

“Please spare me… Wait, could it be—?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hmph. It’s fine. I’ll look at your embarrassing memories next time. I won’t go easy on you when that time comes even if you prostrate yourself before me. That’s right.”
“Anything but that… Wait, could it be…”

最後まで聞けなかった
きゅう、と俺の首を掴んだまま、部屋の外にぽっと放り出される。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
I never finish the question.

Still gripping my neck, she hoists me up and tosses me unceremoniously out of the room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I wasn’t able to ask after all.
She tosses me out of the room by my neck.

遠坂はにっこりと、あの人の悪い笑いを浮かべ
 ばたん、とドアが閉められた。
……こんな格好で廊下に放り出され、呆然と扉を見上げる。

pages.en:
“Emiya? A girl has all sorts of preparations to make. Would you please return to your own room?”

Tohsaka gives me that malicious smile of hers—

and slams the door.

…Thrown into the hallway in this condition, I stare blankly up at it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Emiya-kun? Girls have a lot of preparation to do, so would you mind going back to your own room?”
With that mean grin of hersTohsaka slams the door.
…Pushed into the hallway without my shirt, I stare blankly at the door.

pages.ja:
「……ばか言うな。男にだって色々あるぞ」
まだふらつく頭を抱えて起きあがる。
ドアの向こうの遠坂に何か言い返してやろうかと思ったが、止めておいた。
結局、俺が見たあれが遠坂の何なのかは、聞けずじまいだった。

pages.en:
“…Don't be ridiculous. Men have things to prepare too.”

I clutch my still-spinning head and rise.

For a moment I consider shouting some reply through the door, but decide against it.

In the end, I never learned what the scene I witnessed meant to Tohsaka.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Don’t be stupid. Guys have lots of stuff too.”
I stand up, still clutching my dizzy head.
I want to say something back to Tohsaka on the other side of the door, but I give up.
In the end, I wasn’t able to ask what the scene I saw meant to Tohsaka.

pages.ja:
「……まあ。あれだけイヤがるってコトは、なにか特別な意味のあるコトなんだろうし」
そんな他愛ないことを独りごちながら、部屋に戻っていく。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Well. If she hates it that much, it must have some special significance.”

Muttering that harmless conclusion to myself, I return to my room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Oh well. If she’s that mad about it, it must have some special meaning.”
Muttering stupidly to myself, I go back to my room.

遠坂が追い出したのは口実だったかも知れないが、時間がないのは本当だ。
もう日付は変わっている。
柳洞寺に向かうまで、あと一時間もないだろう。

pages.en:
Throwing me out may have been an excuse, but she was right that we have no time.

Midnight has already passed.

Less than an hour remains before we leave for Ryuudou Temple.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It was probably just an excuse for Tohsaka to kick me out, but it’s true that there’s no time.
The date has already changed.
There’s probably less than an hour left before we head to the temple.

Even though she is making no conscious effort to supply me, it fills my body.

…It might take years to accumulate, but given a sufficient source of supply, her maximum capacity may approach one thousand.

……I’m sure it would take years to fill up her whole capacity, but I bet her maximum capacity could reach a thousand.

“…Incredible. She really is extraordinary.”

It is something I knew, yet only now truly comprehend.

She is depleted at present, and most magi ordinarily maintain their reserves at roughly eighty percent, so Tohsaka currently possesses about four hundred units.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……I’m amazed. She really is amazing.”
It makes me realize her greatness again.
Well, she’s exhausted right now and most magi only keep about 80 percent of their magical energy, so Tohsaka has about 400 magical energy right now.

その例で行くと、最高六回の投影が、遠坂のバックアップで三十回、六十回と出来るようになるんだから。

pages.en:
Even so, it is an immense quantity of magical energy.

One use of Reinforcement costs me an average of two units.

One Projection costs an average of five.

By that measure, Tohsaka's support increases my maximum of six Projections to thirty—or even sixty.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But that’s still a huge amount.
I use about two magical energy to use one strengthening magic,
and about five magical energy to use one projection magic.
Using that example, I can use my projection magic dozens of times now when I could only do it six times before.

All that remains—

“…One more hour. Until then, I need to let my body rest.”

I will recover my strength and spirit for the decisive battle at Ryuudou Temple.

…Every preparation is complete.

For Tohsaka, who gave me her Magic Crest and opened her heart to me, I will meet this final night in perfect condition—
